          path: artifacts/
          if-no-files-found: ignore

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1

FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:11.0 AS build
WORKDIR /source
ARG SOURCE_REVISION=
COPY .editorconfig Directory.Build.props Directory.Packages.props global.json ./
COPY src/MyBlazorPlayground.Domain/MyBlazorPlayground.Domain.csproj src/MyBlazorPlayground.Domain/
COPY src/MyBlazorPlayground.Data/MyBlazorPlayground.Data.csproj src/MyBlazorPlayground.Data/
COPY src/MyBlazorPlayground.Web/MyBlazorPlayground.Web.csproj src/MyBlazorPlayground.Web/
RUN dotnet restore src/MyBlazorPlayground.Web/MyBlazorPlayground.Web.csproj
COPY src/ src/
RUN dotnet publish src/MyBlazorPlayground.Web/MyBlazorPlayground.Web.csproj \
        --configuration Release \
        --no-restore \
        --output /app \
        -p:UseAppHost=false \
        -p:SourceRevisionId="${SOURCE_REVISION}"

FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:11.0 AS runtime
WORKDIR /app
RUN apt-get update \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends tzdata curl \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
COPY --from=build /app .
ENV ASPNETCORE_URLS=http://+:8080 \
    ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production \
    DOTNET_EnableDiagnostics=0
EXPOSE 8080
USER $APP_UID
HEALTHCHECK --interval=15s --timeout=5s --start-period=60s --retries=8 CMD curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8080/health/ready || exit 1
ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "MyBlazorPlayground.Web.dll"]

# my blazor playground

A project tracker for small self-organizing teams, a shared house hunting notebook, and a handful of shared toys, in one Blazor app over PostgreSQL. It lives behind a Cloudflare quick tunnel on the same box as MyRestaurant.

- **Work** (`/work`, needs an account): projects with members and editors, a ranked backlog, sprints, a board, stories, tasks, bugs and epics, Markdown descriptions and comments with pasted screenshots and attachments stored in PostgreSQL, and a change history per item. Mobile first.
- **Homes** (`/homes`, no account): paste links from Zillow, Redfin, Realtor.com or anywhere, fill in details together, comment. Everything is stored in PostgreSQL and in each browser, which sync with each other (from nest).
- **Toys** (no account): board, postcard, canvas, slots, latency test and reader, shared live and kept in memory (from chaos).
- **Roles**: the first administrator is created at `/setup` with a one-time code from the server log. Anyone can edit; only project editors (or home editors) and administrators can delete, deletions go to a trash, only administrators delete for good, and all of it is in the audit log.

## Run it on a server (no .NET SDK needed)

```
scripts/instance.sh up          # build, start, open a quick tunnel, print the URL and the setup code
scripts/instance.sh setup-code  # the code for /setup, until setup is done
scripts/instance.sh url         # the current tunnel URL
scripts/instance.sh status | logs [web|postgres|tunnel] [-f] | backup | restore <file> | down | reset --yes
```

Needs podman with podman-compose (or docker with compose). It uses `127.0.0.1:8090` and `127.0.0.1:5433`, compose project `myblazorplayground` and container `myblazorplayground-tunnel`, so it runs next to MyRestaurant. The first run writes `.env` with a random database password; keep it.

## Develop

```
scripts/dev.sh                  # postgres in a container, dotnet watch on http://127.0.0.1:5090
scripts/test.sh [--no-db] [--no-js]
scripts/export.sh               # docs/llm/dump.txt
```

Requires the .NET 11 SDK (RC 3 or later), Node.js 22 or later for the JavaScript tests, and podman or docker for the database. The containers use stable .NET 11 and PostgreSQL 18.

## Layout

| Path | What |
| --- | --- |
| `src/MyBlazorPlayground.Domain` | Rules without I/O: rich text, passwords, access policy |
| `src/MyBlazorPlayground.Data` | PostgreSQL stores (Npgsql and Dapper) and SQL migrations |
| `src/MyBlazorPlayground.Web` | The site: `Work`, `Nest`, `Chaos`, `Identity`, `Administration` |
| `tests/` | xUnit v3 (domain, data against PostgreSQL, web) and Vitest |
| `scripts/` | Instance, development, test and export scripts |
| `docs/adr/` | Architecture decision records |

## Configuration

Environment variables, or `.env` for the containers:

| Variable | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `ConnectionStrings__Playground` | set by compose from `POSTGRES_*` |
| `Site__Name`, `Site__TimeZone`, `Site__SourceUrl` | `my blazor playground`, `America/New_York`, this repository |
| `Site__AllowedOrigins__0` | none; the request host is always allowed |
| `Work__MaxAttachmentBytes` | 99614720 (95 MiB, under Cloudflare's 100 MB request limit) |
| `Chaos__*`, `Nest__*` | limits of the toys and homes |

# 0002 Three projects, feature folders

Status: accepted

- `MyBlazorPlayground.Domain`: rules with no I/O: rich text rendering, password hashing, setup codes, account and work rules, the access policy, file names and image sniffing. No package references.
- `MyBlazorPlayground.Data`: PostgreSQL through Npgsql and Dapper. One class per aggregate (`PersonStore`, `ProjectStore`, `WorkItemStore`, …), the migration runner and `Deletions`. Knows nothing about HTTP.
- `MyBlazorPlayground.Web`: Blazor, endpoints and application services, by feature: `Identity`, `Work`, `Nest` (homes), `Chaos` (toys), `Administration`, `Persistence`, shared `Infrastructure`. Each feature registers itself (`AddWork`, `AddNest`, …) so `Program.cs` only composes.
- Chaos and nest were merged in rather than referenced: their shared infrastructure (outboxes, token buckets, hub guard, origin policy, security headers) was identical and now lives once in `Infrastructure`, driven by `SiteOptions`. Their feature limits keep their own `Chaos__*` and `Nest__*` sections.
- Components keep chaos and nest's paths (`Components/Islands`, `Components/Pages`, `wwwroot/js`) so their JavaScript modules and relative imports work unchanged.

# 0003 Static forms for work and accounts, islands for live pages

Status: accepted

- Accounts, administration and the project tracker are static server-side rendering with plain `<form method="post">` and `EditForm`, enhanced by Blazor when its script is loaded. They need no circuit, so they keep working over a slow or flaky quick tunnel and they work without JavaScript.
- Each row action is its own small form with a unique `@formname` (`up-12`, `restore-<id>`). After an action the page reloads its data and renders the result; enhanced forms keep the URL and history clean.
- Homes and the toys keep their interactive islands (ADR `homes/0009`, `toys/0007`).
- Progressive enhancement: `App.razor.js` mounts `wwwroot/work/editor.js` on `[data-editor]` (paste and drop uploads, preview, Ctrl+Enter) and `wwwroot/work/board.js` on `[data-board]` (drag and drop, status change on select). Without them, every action still works through the forms.
- Mobile first: board columns scroll and snap sideways below 48 rem, buttons and inputs are at least 44 px tall (small row buttons 34 px), nothing scrolls the page sideways from 320 px up.
- Form models give missing values their defaults in their setters, because form binding assigns every property, including the ones a form did not post.

# 0004 PostgreSQL, Dapper and our own migration runner

Status: accepted

- PostgreSQL is the only store. Dapper maps rows to classes with `init` properties; `DefaultTypeMap.MatchNamesWithUnderscores` maps `snake_case` columns.
- Migrations are numbered SQL files embedded in `MyBlazorPlayground.Data` (`Migrations/0001_initial.sql`). `MigrationRunner` applies the missing ones in order, each in its own transaction, under a PostgreSQL advisory lock, and records them in `schema_migration`. It retries for two minutes while the database is starting. No migration library: the runner is fifty lines.
- Migrations run before the host starts (`StartupTasks`), so nothing (including the Data Protection key ring) touches the database before its schema exists.
- Ids are UUIDv7 from `Guid.CreateVersion7()`; they sort by creation time, which nest relies on. UUIDv7 is not ordered within one millisecond, so item history and the audit log are ordered by an identity column (`seq`) instead.
- Dates are passed as text and cast in SQL, and returned with `to_char`, so nothing depends on how a driver maps `date`. Timestamps are set by `now()` in SQL.
- Multi-step changes and every deletion run in one transaction together with their audit row.
- Attachments are stored in `attachment_chunk` rows of 1 MiB (`STORAGE EXTERNAL`, no recompression). Upload and download stream chunk by chunk, so memory stays flat whatever the file size, and no single value approaches PostgreSQL's 1 GB limit.
- Data Protection keys (antiforgery and sign-in cookies) live in `data_protection_key`, so a restart or a new container keeps everyone signed in and one database dump is a complete backup. They are not encrypted at rest; the database is.

# 0005 Accounts, sign-in and setup

Status: accepted

- Cookie authentication (`playground.auth`, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Secure over HTTPS, 14 days sliding). No email, no external providers, no passkeys: quick tunnel hostnames change, which would orphan passkeys.
- Passwords: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512, 210,000 iterations, 16-byte salt, stored as `pbkdf2-sha512$<iterations>$<salt>$<hash>`. Raising the iteration count rehashes on the next sign-in. Built into .NET, so no package. At least 12 characters, not the user name, not one repeated character.
- Every cookie carries the account's security stamp. At most once a minute per browser the stamp, the disabled flag, the display name and the administrator role are checked against the database. A password change or disabling an account rotates the stamp and signs the account out everywhere; role changes reach the cookie within a minute without a sign-out.
- Sign-in, registration, setup and password changes are throttled per network address and per user name (10 burst, one every 10 s). Unknown user names still pay for a hash so timing does not reveal them.
- `/setup` creates the first administrator. It needs a one-time code that is generated at start-up while no administrator exists and printed to the server log (`scripts/instance.sh setup-code`). The public URL is reachable by anyone, so the code is what stops a stranger from claiming the site. A table lock makes a second concurrent setup fail.
- Registration is open by default and can be closed by an administrator.

# 0006 Roles, deleting and the audit log

Status: accepted

| Who | Can |
| --- | --- |
| Anyone | Use homes and the toys; add and edit there |
| Signed-in account | Create projects; open projects it belongs to |
| Project member | Add and edit items, sprints and comments in the project |
| Project editor | Also delete and restore in the project, manage members |
| Home page editor | Delete and restore entries on that home |
| Administrator | Everything, everywhere; grant roles; delete for good |

- The rules are one class, `AccessPolicy`, with tests. Pages ask it; services check it again.
- Deleting is soft: `deleted_at` and `deleted_by` are set and the record disappears everywhere. Editors restore from the project settings; administrators from the site trash.
- Only administrators delete for good, and only from the trash. A project's permanent deletion cascades to everything in it.
- Every soft delete, restore and permanent deletion writes an `audit_event` in the same transaction. So do role grants, member changes, registrations, setup, password changes and failed sign-ins.
- A project always has an editor and the site always has an active administrator; the last one cannot be demoted, removed or disabled.
- Comments are edited by their author or an editor. Anything else in a project can be edited by any member.
- Home pages have no owner, so their editors are granted by an administrator per home key (`home:zillow:29747113`). Any key of a merged home counts.
- The toys keep nothing past a restart and have no delete (ADR 0008).

# 0007 Homes keep everything in PostgreSQL

Status: accepted. Supersedes the in-memory capacity in `homes/0004`.

- Every accepted entry, posted or offered back by a browser, is written to `nest_entry` by `NestJournal`, a background writer with retries, so posting never waits for the database. If the database stays down the entry is still in every browser that saw it and is offered back later.
- On start-up the newest `Nest__Capacity` entries (default 100,000) are loaded into `NestService`, which then works exactly as before. Browsers still keep their own copy in IndexedDB and still offer back what the server lacks.
- Deleting an entry marks it deleted in the database, removes it from memory, and remembers its id as a tombstone. Snapshots and deltas carry `deleted` ids; browsers drop those from memory and IndexedDB. Offers of a deleted id are refused, so a browser that was offline cannot bring it back.
- Deleting for good clears the entry's content but keeps the row as a tombstone (`purged_at`), for the same reason.
- Restoring puts the entry back into memory and every browser receives it as an addition.

# 0008 The toys keep their in-memory design

Status: accepted

- Board, postcard, canvas, slots, latency and read are ported from chaos unchanged in behavior: the server keeps a small window in memory, browsers keep history in IndexedDB and offer it back after a restart (ADRs in `toys/`).
- They do not use the database. Forgetting is part of what they are, and their windows are sized for memory, not for storage.
- Their limits (`Chaos__*`) and protocols are as before. Shared connection and request limits moved to `Site__*`.
- `wwwroot/nytimes.txt` is not part of this repository; without it `/read` shows a notice.

# 0009 Markdown with pasted screenshots

Status: accepted

- Descriptions and comments are stored as Markdown text and rendered on the server by `RichText`, which escapes everything first and then builds a fixed set of elements: paragraphs, line breaks, headings, bold, italic, strikethrough, inline and fenced code, lists, task lists, quotes, rules, links and images. There is no HTML pass-through and no third-party sanitizer, so there is nothing to bypass; tests check that only those tags and attributes come out.
- Links may be `http`, `https`, `mailto` or a local path. Images are shown only from local paths, so pasted screenshots work and remote images cannot track readers (the CSP would block them anyway). `#12` links to item 12 of the same project.
- Pasting or dropping files into an editor uploads each one immediately to `POST /work/{key}/attachments` (raw body, file name in `X-File-Name`, antiforgery token in a header) and inserts `![name](url)` or `[name](url)` at the cursor. Screenshots from the clipboard are named by time. Pasted HTML is converted to Markdown in the browser.
- Uploaded files are served from `/work/files/{id}/{name}` to project members only. Images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, sniffed from the bytes) are shown inline; everything else downloads as `application/octet-stream` with `nosniff` and a sandboxing CSP.
- The size limit is `Work__MaxAttachmentBytes`, default 95 MiB, because Cloudflare refuses request bodies over 100 MB on the free plan. Storage itself has no practical limit (ADR 0004).
- Preview sends the text to `POST /work/{key}/preview`, which returns the same server rendering.

# 0010 Quick tunnels, side by side with MyRestaurant

Status: accepted

- The site lives behind a Cloudflare quick tunnel permanently. The URL can change and the site can be down; nothing in the site depends on its public URL. All links are relative.
- It runs on the same host as MyRestaurant without clashing: compose project `myblazorplayground`, web on `127.0.0.1:8090`, PostgreSQL on `127.0.0.1:5433` (MyRestaurant uses 8080, 8443 and 5432), its own volume, image name and tunnel container (`myblazorplayground-tunnel`).
- `scripts/instance.sh up` builds, starts PostgreSQL and the site, waits for `/health/ready`, starts cloudflared with host networking and prints the URL and, before setup, the setup code. `url`, `status`, `logs`, `backup`, `restore`, `down` and `reset` cover the rest.
- `.env` is created from `.env.example` on first use with a random database password. Every variable is assigned there because some podman-compose versions ignore `${VAR:-default}`.
- No `depends_on` waits for health: the migration runner retries the database for two minutes instead.
- Inside containers everything is stable: `sdk:11.0` and `aspnet:11.0`, PostgreSQL 18. PostgreSQL 19 reaches general availability on 2026-11-19; moving to it is the image tag in `compose.yaml`, `scripts/test.sh` and the workflow, plus a dump and restore of existing data.
- Locally, `global.json` accepts the 11.0 RC 3 SDK and anything newer in the band.
- The web container runs as the image's non-root `app` user and writes nothing to disk.
- Backups are one `pg_dump`, because keys live in the database too.

# 0011 Headers, CSP and forms

Status: accepted

- The chaos policy stays: `default-src 'self'`, scripts and styles only from this site, no inline scripts or `style` attributes, `img-src 'self' blob:`, `connect-src 'self'` plus the latency endpoints, `frame-ancestors 'none'`, `form-action 'self'`. Progress bars use classes, not inline widths.
- Chaos and nest replaced antiforgery with a cookieless stub because they had no forms. This site has forms, so the standard antiforgery cookie and tokens are back. JSON endpoints validate the token from the `RequestVerificationToken` header.
- `/_blazor` only accepts WebSockets from this origin (or `Site__AllowedOrigins`), with per-client and total connection limits. Requests are rate limited per client address after `X-Forwarded-For`.
- Return URLs after sign-in are accepted only when they are local paths.
- Rendered user content goes through `RichText` or Razor encoding only.

# 0004 Entries, UUIDv7 ids and the handshake

Status: accepted

- Everything users add is an immutable entry: `link` (a URL), `fact` (one or more detail fields) or `comment` (text). Each carries the keys of its home (ADR 0005). Nothing is edited or deleted; a newer fact replaces an older value.
- The server mints every id with `Uuid7.After` from its own clock, so ids are unique, increasing and sortable as strings. Clients never mint ids, so adding needs a connection.
- The server keeps every entry in PostgreSQL and the newest `Nest__Capacity` (default 100,000) in memory (ADR 0007).
- Handshake, in this order:
  1. The browser calls `Join`. The server sends a snapshot of ids only, plus its capacity.
  2. The browser fetches the entries it lacks, 50 ids per call.
  3. The browser offers entries the server lacks, newest first, at most the capacity, and only ones newer than the server's oldest when the server is full. Offers are sent in chunks under 24 KB of JSON.
- An offered entry is accepted only if its id is a valid UUIDv7, not in the future, older than the server's start, and the entry is already in normal form (rebuilding it gives the same entry). The server keeps its own copy on id ties, stores what it accepts, and refuses ids that were deleted (ADR 0007). Offers beyond the capacity per circuit are ignored.
- The start-time rule rejects forged recent entries: anything stamped after the server started came from this server, so if the server does not have it, it is forged or already evicted.
- A link whose key the server already has on a link entry returns `exists` and the home's key instead of a new entry.
- The same comment or fact on the same keys as one of the 20 newest entries is refused as a repeat.
- Interop uses `JsonElement` arguments and results with internal records, so no wire type is public.

# 0005 Listing keys, union-find merge, newest value wins

Status: accepted

- A home has no id of its own. It is the set of keys its entries carry: `zillow:<zpid>`, `redfin:<id>`, `realtor:m<id>`, `address:<zip>-<street>` and `url:<hash>` (ADR 0006).
- An entry's keys are the key derived from its own content (the link, or the street and ZIP of a fact) plus the keys of the home it was added to, at most 8, sorted.
- Merge: union-find over keys. Two entries that share any key belong to the same home, directly or through others. The result does not depend on order, so every browser and the server agree on the same entries.
- The page address is the key with the highest rank (Zillow, Redfin, Realtor.com, address, link, then text order). Any key of the home opens the same page.
- Details: for each field, the value from the entry with the newest id wins. An empty value clears the field. The previous different value is shown as "was …".
- Comments are listed oldest first. Links are shown once per key, newest URL.
- An address key is derived only from a fact that has both street and ZIP. Saving any address field sends all five so the key is consistent.
- Merging cannot be undone. A wrong link or address joins two homes for everyone. Accepted: there are no accounts to decide who may split them.
- The same algorithm exists in C# (`ListingIndex`, for the prerender) and JavaScript (`merge.js`). `tests/fixtures/listings.json` pins both to the same result.

# 0006 Reading listing links and addresses

Status: accepted

- The first `http(s)://` URL in the pasted text is used, so text shared from an app works. The URL ends at the first character outside printable ASCII, a space, `"`, `'`, `<` or `>`; trailing `.,;:!?)]}` are dropped. At most 2,048 characters.
- Query strings and fragments are dropped everywhere. Hosts are lowercased; user info in the host is rejected.
- Zillow: `<digits>_zpid` anywhere in the path. Redfin: `/home/<digits>`. Realtor.com: `_M<digits>-<digits>`. Leading zeros are dropped. These links are stored as `https://` with the original host and path.
- Other links: `url:` plus the 64-bit FNV-1a hash of host without `www.` or port plus the path without trailing slashes. Scheme does not count.
- Addresses: ASCII letters are lowercased, everything that is not an ASCII letter or digit separates words, common street words are shortened to USPS forms (`street` → `st`, `route` → `rte`, `north` → `n`, …). `apt`, `apartment`, `unit`, `suite`, `ste` and `#` start the unit; an explicit unit field wins. Key: `address:<zip>-<street words>[-unit-<unit words>]`, at most 100 characters.
- Non-ASCII letters are separators, not folded. Rare in US addresses; it keeps C# and JavaScript identical without Unicode tables.
- Regular expressions avoid case-insensitive flags and use `\z` in .NET, because the engines differ on Unicode case folding and on `$` before a newline.
- The browser also guesses an address from Zillow, Redfin and Realtor.com paths to prefill the details form. Zillow slugs mix street and city, so that guess is marked for checking. Guesses are never saved without the user pressing Save.
- `tests/fixtures/links.json` and `addresses.json` are run by both test suites.
- Nest never fetches the listing sites. There is no API access, and fetching would add third-party requests and terms-of-use questions.

# 0007 Details fields and their normal form

Status: accepted

| Field | Normal form |
| --- | --- |
| Price, HOA per month, taxes per year | Whole dollars. `$`, commas, spaces, `_` ignored. `450k`, `1.25m` accepted. At most 11 digits. |
| Bedrooms | 0–99 |
| Bathrooms | 0–99 with up to two decimals, trailing zeros dropped |
| Square feet | 1–10,000,000 |
| Year built | 1600–2100 |
| Status, type | One of a fixed list, matched ignoring ASCII case |
| State | Two letters, uppercased |
| ZIP code | Five digits; ZIP+4 is cut to five |
| Lot size, parking, heating and cooling, MLS number, street, unit, city | Text: control characters removed, spaces collapsed, cut to 20–120 characters |

- The browser validates before sending and shows the reason next to the field. The server applies the same rules and refuses an entry with any invalid value. `tests/fixtures/fields.json` pins both.
- Only changed fields are sent, except the address group (ADR 0005).
- Values are self-reported and unverified. There is no history editing.
- Comments: up to 4,000 UTF-16 code units, cut on grapheme boundaries, three or more blank lines collapsed, emoji kept.

# 0008 IndexedDB, drafts and clearing

Status: accepted

- Database `nest`, store `entries`, key path `id`, values are entries plus `mine: true` for entries posted from this browser.
- Schema changes are numbered migrations in `wwwroot/js/store.js`; `onupgradeneeded` runs every step from the stored version. A database from a newer schema (`VersionError`) is deleted and recreated, since the server and other browsers can refill it. Other tabs close their connection on `versionchange`.
- Cap: 20,000 entries. After each write the oldest are deleted with one key-range delete and dropped from memory.
- All entries are loaded into memory once per page load to build the home list. 20,000 short entries fit comfortably on a phone.
- Unsent comments are kept per home in `localStorage` (`nest-draft:<key>`) until sent. The "only homes I added to" filter is `nest-mine-only`. The theme is `playground-theme`, shared by the whole site.
- Entries deleted by an editor or administrator arrive as `deleted` ids in snapshots and deltas; the browser drops them from memory and IndexedDB (ADR 0007).
- Solid border: the server has the entry. Dotted: only browsers have it. A home card is dotted when none of its entries are on the server.
- The About page deletes the database, the drafts and the filter, keeps the theme, and empties the in-memory copy. It does not touch the server or other browsers. The next visit fills the database from the server.
- Without IndexedDB the site still works, without history.

# 0009 Per-client outboxes over the circuit

Status: accepted

- Transport is the Blazor circuit: JavaScript calls `[JSInvokable]` methods (`Join`, `Ping`, `Fetch`, `Offer`, `Post`); the server calls the module's `apply`. No separate SignalR hub.
- Each island owns a bounded `Outbox<NestUpdate>` drained by one pump that sends batches in order and waits for the browser. A full outbox, a failed call or a 20 s stall drops the subscriber.
- The pump waits until the module is attached, because `Join` can arrive before `attach` returns to .NET.
- Subscribing enqueues the snapshot under the same lock as updates, so nothing is missed or duplicated.
- Deltas carry `version` and `previous`; a gap triggers a fresh `Join`. `apply` does not wait for fetching and offering, so the outbox never stalls on them.
- The browser pings every 25 s and rejoins when the server says it was dropped, and after every reconnect.

# 0004 UUIDv7 ids and handshake rules

Status: accepted

- The server creates every id with `Guid.CreateVersion7` from its own clock. Clients never mint ids. Timestamps are read from the id.
- The id string sorts in time order, so it is also the IndexedDB key and the sort key everywhere. Two posts in the same millisecond sort in random order; that is accepted.
- Handshake: the client offers its 50 newest local messages, newest first, in chunks under 24 KB so no SignalR message exceeds the 32 KB limit. The server considers at most 50 per circuit.
- An offered message is accepted only if its id is a valid UUIDv7, its time is not in the future, its time is before the server started, and its text is already normalized, and its `meta` is absent or already normalized (ADR 0022). Then it is merged; the server keeps the newest 50 and keeps its own copy on id ties.
- The start-time rule rejects forged recent messages: anything stamped after the server started came from this server, so if the server does not have it, it is forged or already evicted. It costs posts made to an old instance during a rolling deploy; those stay in local history.
- Posts: 500 UTF-16 code units after normalization, cut on grapheme boundaries; the same text as one of the 10 newest messages is refused.

# 0006 Canvas coordinates, epochs and storage

Status: accepted

- The page is square (`aspect-ratio: 1`). Points are normalized to 0–1 and sent as integers 0–4095. The brush width is 0.6% of the canvas side, so every device draws the same picture.
- The backing store is CSS size times `devicePixelRatio`. A `ResizeObserver` and a `resolution` media query trigger a full redraw from stored points.
- Input: pointer events with pointer capture, `touch-action: none`, primary pointer only, left mouse button only, coalesced events when available, points closer than 3 units dropped.
- Palm rejection: touches wider or taller than 40 CSS px are ignored, and so is any touch within 1.5 s of pen input.
- Batches go out every 50 ms, at most 256 points, one call in flight. A stroke ends at 2,000 points.
- Every reset increments an epoch. Batches tagged with an old epoch are refused, so strokes in flight during a reset vanish.
- Late joiners get a snapshot of every stored stroke. The store keeps 20,000 points and evicts the oldest finished strokes first. Clients that already drew an evicted stroke keep showing it until the next reset.
- Every stroke and every reset gets a server UUIDv7 (`Uuid7.After` keeps them strictly increasing), so a stroke sorts after the reset it follows. `Draw` replies `"<result> <stroke id>"`.
- Browsers keep finished strokes in IndexedDB `chaos-canvas`: store `strokes` (`{ id, points: Uint16Array }`, cap 10,000, oldest deleted first) and store `meta` (`{ key: 'reset', id }`). A reset deletes every stroke up to its id; strokes older than the stored reset are never saved.
- Snapshots carry `reset`, `started` (server start, Unix ms) and `room` (free points). After each snapshot the browser offers its stored reset if newer than the server's and older than `started`, then its newest 500 strokes newer than both resets, older than `started`, unknown to the server and within `room`, in chunks under 24 KB.
- The server accepts an offered stroke only if it is a valid UUIDv7 from before the server started, newer than the current reset, unknown and well formed, and only while it fits: offers never evict. Accepted strokes go to everyone as a `merge` update. An adopted reset drops older strokes, bumps the epoch and sends everyone a fresh snapshot. A reset made on this server always wins over remembered ones.
- Per circuit: 500 offered strokes, `CanvasMaxPoints` offered points, 4 offered resets.

# 0007 Per-client outboxes over the circuit

Status: accepted

- Transport is the Blazor circuit itself: JS calls `[JSInvokable]` methods, the server calls the module's `apply`. No separate SignalR hub and no extra JavaScript client.
- Each island owns a bounded channel (`Outbox<T>`) drained by one pump that sends batches in order and waits for the browser to finish each batch. A full outbox, a failed call or a 20 s stall drops the subscriber.
- The pump waits until the island's module has been attached. JavaScript can call `Join` before `attach` has returned to .NET, and an earlier send would fault the outbox.
- Subscribing enqueues a snapshot under the same lock as updates, so nothing is missed or duplicated.
- Board deltas carry `version` and `previous`; a gap triggers a fresh snapshot. Canvas updates carry an offset per stroke; a gap triggers a fresh snapshot. Slots and latency deltas use the board rules; a latency `state` update only carries `running`, and latency snapshots and changed deltas carry `boards` (ADR 0020).
- The browser pings every 25 s and resubscribes when the server says it was dropped, and resubscribes after every reconnect.

# 0019 Shared slot machine

Status: accepted

- `/slots` hosts `SlotIsland`. Results are `{ id, text }` like board messages: UUIDv7 from the server clock, five symbols from `0-9A-Z`, newest 50 kept, same offer, merge and delta rules (`MessageWindow`).
- The server draws the result with `RandomNumberGenerator` when it accepts a press, then refuses every press until `SpinMilliseconds` (default 4,000) has passed. Busy presses are checked before the per-client bucket.
- `SlotDrawSymbols` (default all 36) limits the symbols drawn. Tests only: `7` makes every spin `77777`. Invalid values fail options validation; the service falls back to all symbols.
- The accepting delta and late-joiner snapshots carry `spin: { id, remaining }`. Clients animate for `remaining` ms from receipt, then add the result to the feed. Because receipt is later than the server clock, a client's button only re-enables after the server lock has expired.
- A spin that arrives while an older animation runs finishes the older one at once.
- Winners: three or more of one symbol anywhere, or five strictly ascending or descending in ASCII order (digits before letters). 1,201,320 of 36⁵ = 60,466,176, about 1 in 50.3. Ascending or descending runs of neighbours in `0-9A-Z` with no gaps (`ABCDE`, `789AB`, `43210`) are sequences, not straights: 32 each way, 64 total, 1 in 944,784. No wraparound (`YZ012` loses). Straights are the remaining 376,960 each way. Rules exist in `SlotRules.cs` and `SlotIsland.razor.js`; both are tested with the same cases.
- Winners window: newest `SlotWinnerCapacity` (default 500). Snapshots and deltas carry `winnersAdded` and `winnersRemoved` beside `added` and `removed`, under the same version. Clients hold back the spinning result from the winners list until its reels stop.
- Jackpots: four of a kind, five of a kind or a sequence, 6,400 results, about 1 in 9,448. Kept in a third list that never evicts. Drawn jackpots are always added. Offered jackpots are added only while the list holds fewer than `SlotJackpotCapacity` (default 10,000), so forged offers cannot grow it without bound. Snapshots carry every jackpot in `jackpotsAdded`; deltas carry new ones. There is no `jackpotsRemoved`.
- A jackpot that settles on screen adds `jackpot` to the machine for 8 s: verdict `Jackpot! <kind>`, cabinet glow, fast lights, CSS confetti (24 prerendered spans). Reduced motion keeps the glow and verdict only. Screen readers hear `Jackpot!`. Late joiners and instant finishes do not celebrate.
- After restarts, clients offer their newest 500 local winners through `OfferWinners` (winners and jackpots only) and up to 500 local jackpots through `OfferJackpots` (jackpots only), each with its own per-circuit budget. Chunks stay under 24 KB.
- Local storage: IndexedDB `chaos-slots` v2. `spins` is capped at 10,000 like the board. `jackpots` (added by migration 2) is never pruned. On each visit jackpots found in `spins` are copied into it, which also migrates v1 data.
- Every winner is a `<details>`. Its odds panel is built in the browser on first open from `lesson()` in `SlotIsland.razor.js`, the only place the probability text lives. Counts are formulas checked against an exhaustive search over a contiguous six-symbol alphabet (`89ABCD`), so sequences occur.
- No identity. `Press` returns the new id, `busy` or `slow` to the caller only. The browser marks its own results as `mine` in IndexedDB.
- Successful presses are counted in `localStorage` (`chaos-slots-presses`). At 10 the auto spin toggle appears; it presses 200–1,000 ms after each settle, keeps going while the tab is hidden (browsers may throttle its timers there), and is off on every page load.
- Reels are DOM strips moved with the Web Animations API by percentage of their own height, so no layout reads. Reduced motion swaps symbols without movement. Nothing uses inline style attributes, so the CSP is unchanged.

# 0020 Shared latency test

Status: accepted

- `/latency` hosts `LatencyIsland`. `LatencyCatalog` lists the endpoints: this site's `/time` (browser only), large public sites and 17 AWS DynamoDB `/ping` regions. All are anonymous GETs.
- `Begin` is refused (`busy`) while a test runs or within `LatencyGapSeconds` of the last start, then per client (`wait <seconds>`) for `LatencyCooldownSeconds`. A client is a network address (ADR 0008), so devices behind one NAT share the cooldown; the browser says so. Browser storage cannot enforce a limit, so `chaos-latency-next` is only a countdown hint. Accepted starts reply `ok <id> <cooldown>` and broadcast `running`.
- The server probes in the background (`HttpLatencyProbe`): one warm-up request, then the fastest of 3 time-to-headers, 6 endpoints at a time, 4 s per request, `LatencyBudgetSeconds` overall. `LatencyServerProbe=false` turns it off.
- The browser does the same with `fetch` (`no-cors`, `no-store`, no credentials, no referrer) and sends `Finish(id, ms[])`, -1 for failures. The server waits up to the budget plus 15 s, then publishes either way.
- A result is `{ id, text }` with text `key=browser,server;…` in integer ms, empty for none. Offers must re-serialize to the same text. Server keeps 50, browsers 10,000 (`chaos-latency`), same merge rules as slots.
- Ranking: a run's browser or server median counts only when at least half its endpoints answered on that side (`LatencyRun.Rank`, `rank()` in JS, tested with the same cases).
- Leaderboards (`LatencyLeaders`): jackpot winners (a counted median under 10 ms) and losers (100 ms or more), newest `LatencyJackpotCapacity` (default 50) each; and the `LatencyRankCapacity` (default 10) lowest and highest counted medians per side, ties to the older run. Every measured or offered run is a candidate.
- Snapshots carry `boards`: six ordered id lists (`fastJackpots`, `slowJackpots`, `browserFastest`, `browserSlowest`, `serverFastest`, `serverSlowest`) and `runs`, the texts the client has not seen. Deltas carry `boards` only when a list changes, with only new texts. Browsers save leader runs to local history.
- After a restart, browsers read every local run and offer their 10 best and 10 worst counted medians per side through `OfferLeaders` (40 per circuit, boards only, same validation as offers). Offers are trusted like slot jackpots; the caps bound forgeries.
- The page lists Results, then Leaderboard, then Jackpots.
- No identity: results hold only timings. The browser marks its own as `mine`. Test count (`chaos-latency-runs`) and next allowed time (`chaos-latency-next`) are in `localStorage`; 10 tests unlock auto run, which tests whenever allowed, including in hidden tabs.

# 0021 Server clock in the footer

Status: accepted

- `MainLayout` renders the server's local time, Unix ms and UTC offset into `<time id="server-clock" data-permanent>`. No circuit is needed.
- `App.razor.js` turns that into an offset from `performance.now()`, using the navigation timing window (`requestStart`–`responseStart`) as the error bound, and ticks once per second. The device's wall clock is never shown.
- It resyncs from `GET /time` (`{ unixMs, offsetMinutes }`, `no-store`) on load, every 10 minutes, when the tab becomes visible and when wall time and monotonic time drift apart by over 2 s (sleep). A sample replaces the current one if its error is smaller than the current error plus 100 ppm of its age; forced resyncs always replace it.

# 0022 Optional location and browser details on board messages

Status: accepted

- Postcards use the same fields, rules and setting (ADR 0023).

- Opt-in. `#compose-share` appears only when `navigator.geolocation` exists. Ticking it calls `getCurrentPosition`; the browser prompt is the consent. Without permission nothing changes.
- Default state: on when the Permissions API reports `granted` and `localStorage` `chaos-board-share` is not `off`; off when denied. Unticking stores `off`. A permission change to `denied` unticks it. Clearing local history removes the key.
- On send, `BoardIsland` asks the module for `meta()` (15 s server timeout, `maximumAge` 60 s, 10 s position timeout). Failure sends the message without details.
- `collectMeta` reads only the browser: coordinates, accuracy, altitude, heading, speed, fix time, `Intl` time zone, locale, calendar, numbering system, UTC offset, local time, languages, user agent, client hints brands, platform, mobile, vendor, webdriver, Do Not Track, GPC, PDF viewer, screen, available screen, viewport, pixel ratio, color depth, orientation, threads, memory, touch points, pointer, color scheme, reduced motion, contrast, online, connection type, downlink, RTT, save data.
- No reverse geocoding, no third-party requests. The server adds nothing: no IP, no headers.
- Wire and storage: `BoardMessage.meta` is an ordered list of `{ key, value }` strings, omitted when null. `MessageMeta` keeps known keys only, in catalog order, first occurrence wins, strips control characters, trims, cuts to a per-key length and range-checks numeric keys. Without valid latitude and longitude the list is dropped. Offers carry `meta` and must already be normalized.
- Values are self-reported and unverified.
- Labels live in `MessageMeta.Fields` and `META_FIELDS`; tests pin the same key order in both.
- `Submit` returns the new message; the island calls `sent(id)`, which clears the composer and recounts in the browser before Blazor re-renders, then calls `own(id)` so the browser marks it `mine` in IndexedDB and shows `Your message`. The server keeps no ownership. Older messages are unaffected.
- Rendering: collapsed `<details class="meta">` under the text, timestamp-sized and muted, both in the prerender and in the module.

# 0023 Postcards: one long message with images

Status: accepted

- `/postcard` hosts `PostcardIsland`. The server keeps one postcard, the newest; each accepted one replaces it. No jackpots, no winners.
- Limits (`PostcardRules`, mirrored in `PostcardIsland.razor.js`): 5,000 characters (`MessageText` with a longer limit), up to 4 images, PNG, JPEG or GIF, 2 MB each, 4 MB together, at most 4,096 px a side and 4,096² px, GIFs at most 1,000 frames. Text or at least one image is required. A postcard identical to the current one (text and image bytes) is refused.
- Why these numbers: one postcard is at most 4 MB in memory, plus at most `PostcardUploads` (default 2) uploads in flight, well inside 256 MB; 5,000 characters stay under the 32 KB hub message limit even as 3-byte UTF-8.
- Rate: `PostcardBurst` 2, `PostcardsPerSecond` 0.1 per client. Size and count are checked before the rate bucket and before any upload. When every upload slot is taken, image postcards get `busy`.
- Upload: the module handles submit itself and calls `Send(text, images, meta)`. Images go as `DotNet.createJSStreamReference(blob)` and are read with `OpenReadStreamAsync`, chunked under the hub limit. No HTTP upload endpoint, so origin checks and limits stay on the circuit.
- The browser drops control characters and lone surrogates before sending. JPEG and PNG over 2 MB or 4,096 px are redrawn on a canvas to 2,048 px JPEG at 0.85, which also applies EXIF rotation. GIFs are sent as they are or refused.
- `ImageSanitizer` decides the type from the bytes, never the name or MIME type, walks the file structure, and rebuilds it: PNG keeps rendering chunks only (no `tEXt`, `zTXt`, `iTXt`, `eXIf`, `tIME`) and refuses unknown critical chunks; JPEG drops `APP1`–`APP15` except ICC and Adobe, and `COM`, then writes a 34-byte EXIF with only the orientation when it was not 1; GIF drops comments, plain text and application extensions other than looping. Anything truncated, unknown or out of range is refused.
- Wire: `PostcardUpdate { kind, version, card }`, `kind` `snapshot` on join and `change` after. A card is `{ id, text, images: [{ type, width, height, length }], meta? }`. Bytes never travel over the circuit to viewers.
- Images: `GET /postcard/images/{id}/{index}` serves the current postcard only, `private, max-age=31536000, immutable`, 404 otherwise. The prerender uses these URLs; the module fetches each image once, checks its length and stores it.
- Local history: database `chaos-postcards` v1, stores `cards` (`{ id, text, images, meta?, mine? }`), `images` (`{ key: "<id>/<index>", id, blob }`) and `state` (`bytes`). 10,000 cards; images up to 256 MB, oldest images evicted first while their text stays. On a quota error the card is saved without images. Missing images show `Image n of m was not kept`. Images are shown from `blob:` URLs, so the CSP allows `img-src 'self' blob:`; URLs are revoked when the feed is redrawn or the island is disposed.
- Feed: the live postcard plus 20 stored ones, a button for 20 more. Every postcard but the live one has a dotted border.
- After a restart (snapshot without a card) the browser offers its newest postcard once per circuit, images included, if all of them are stored. `WouldRestore` checks the UUIDv7 before any upload; the server accepts it only if it is older than the server start and newer than the current postcard, with normalized text and details and clean images.
- Details and `Your message` work as on the board (ADR 0022) and share the `chaos-board-share` setting. The browser marks its own postcards `mine` from the `Send` reply. The reply and the `change` update race (the update usually wins while stream references are released), so `mine` is applied whenever a card enters the feed and on every save, whichever comes first.

# 0024 Random article reader

Status: accepted

- `/read` is a static SSR page with no circuit. `RandomArticle` middleware answers GET/HEAD `/read` with a 302 to a relative `/read/{id}` (`no-store`), so every article has a stable address and enhanced navigation shows the final URL. Not `NavigateTo`: Blazor makes that `Location` absolute from the request `Host`, which behind a proxy can be an internal host. With no articles the page renders a notice instead.
- Source: `wwwroot/nytimes.txt` (`Chaos:ArticlesFile`), plain UTF-8, also served as a static file. Records start with a header between two `=` rules (20 or more, up to 6 header lines). Inside: optional `SUMMARY` paragraph, `ARTICLE`, then a head paragraph (title, optional dek, `By …`, `Published yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm UTC`, source URL, matched from the end) and body paragraphs split by blank lines. Paragraphs whose every line starts with `- `, `• `, `* ` render as lists; other line breaks are kept. A file with no rules is one article.
- Id: first 12 hex digits of SHA-256 of the source URL, or of title and body without one. Stable across reordering and edits elsewhere in the file. The first record wins on duplicate ids.
- `ArticleLibrary` indexes the file once (offset and length per id, about 50 KB for 500 articles), then reads and parses one record per request. It re-indexes when the file's length or modified time changes, treats a missing, unreadable or over-64 MB file as empty, and returns nothing rather than throwing. A record that no longer parses to its id is dropped and the index rebuilt.
- Unknown or removed ids render "Not available" with a link to a random article (200, so the history list still renders).
- Reading history lives only in the browser: IndexedDB `chaos-reading` v1, store `articles`, key `id`, values `{ id, title, byline, published, first, last, reads }`, capped at 1,000 by least recent `last`. `App.razor.js` imports `Pages/ReadPage.razor.js` on load and `enhancedload` when `#reading-history` exists. The list is `data-permanent` and only written by that module.
- Typography: serif stack, 17–19 px, line height 1.7, 38 rem measure, hyphenation in the body, solid background behind the text.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Local development: postgres in a container, the site with dotnet watch on the host.
#
#   scripts/dev.sh           start postgres, then dotnet watch on http://127.0.0.1:5090 (Ctrl+C stops the site)
#   scripts/dev.sh --db      start postgres only and print the connection string
#

source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/lib.sh"
LOG_TAG=dev
cd "$ROOT"

detect_engine
ensure_env

password="$(env_value POSTGRES_PASSWORD playground)"
db="$(env_value POSTGRES_DB playground)"

    printf '%s\n' "$ConnectionStrings__Playground"

log "the setup code is printed below on first start; open http://127.0.0.1:5090/setup"
exec dotnet watch --project src/MyBlazorPlayground.Web --launch-profile http

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

PROJECT_PATH="${1:-$SCRIPT_DIR/..}"
OUTPUT_FILE="${2:-docs/llm/dump.txt}"

INCLUDE_EXTENSIONS="cs csproj slnx props targets json razor js mjs css html svg yml yaml sh md toml sql"
INCLUDE_NAMES=".gitignore .gitattributes .editorconfig .dockerignore .env.example Containerfile"
EXCLUDE_NAMES="package-lock.json LICENSE"
EXCLUDE_DIRS="bin obj .vs .git node_modules .vscode .idea TestResults artifacts coverage"
EXCLUDE_PREFIXES="docs/llm/"

PROJECT_PATH="$(cd "$PROJECT_PATH" && pwd)"
cd "$PROJECT_PATH"

case "$OUTPUT_FILE" in
    /*) OUTPUT_PATH="$OUTPUT_FILE" ;;
    *)  OUTPUT_PATH="$PROJECT_PATH/$OUTPUT_FILE" ;;
esac
OUTPUT_DIR="$(dirname "$OUTPUT_PATH")"
mkdir -p "$OUTPUT_DIR"

OUTPUT_REL="${OUTPUT_PATH#"$PROJECT_PATH"/}"

if [ -t 1 ]; then
    GREEN='\033[0;32m'; YELLOW='\033[0;33m'; CYAN='\033[0;36m'; NC='\033[0m'
else
    GREEN=''; YELLOW=''; CYAN=''; NC=''
fi
log() { printf "%b%s%b\n" "$1" "$2" "$NC"; }

sha256_of() {
    if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        sha256sum "$1" | awk '{print $1}'
    elif command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        shasum -a 256 "$1" | awk '{print $1}'
    else
        printf 'unavailable'
    fi
}

mod_time_utc_of() {
    local epoch
    if epoch="$(stat -c '%Y' "$1" 2>/dev/null)"; then
        date -u -d "@$epoch" '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'
    else
        epoch="$(stat -f '%m' "$1")"
        date -u -r "$epoch" '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'
    fi
}

line_count_of() {
    awk 'END { print NR }' "$1"
}

is_included_file() {
    local name="${1##*/}" ext entry
    for entry in $EXCLUDE_NAMES; do
        [ "$name" = "$entry" ] && return 1
    done
    case "$name" in
        .env.example) return 0 ;;
        .env|.env.*) return 1 ;;
    esac
    for entry in $INCLUDE_NAMES; do
        [ "$name" = "$entry" ] && return 0
    done
    ext="${name##*.}"
    [ "$ext" != "$name" ] || return 1
    ext="$(printf '%s' "$ext" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
    for entry in $INCLUDE_EXTENSIONS; do
        [ "$ext" = "$entry" ] && return 0
    done
    return 1
}

is_excluded_path() {
    local path="$1" entry
    for entry in $EXCLUDE_PREFIXES; do
        case "$path" in
            "$entry"*) return 0 ;;
        esac
    done
    for entry in $EXCLUDE_DIRS; do
        case "$path" in
            "$entry"/*|*/"$entry"/*) return 0 ;;
        esac
    done
    return 1
}

is_text() {
    [ ! -s "$1" ] || grep -Iq . "$1"
}

in_git_repo() { git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1; }

render_tree() {
    local -a parts prev
    local rel n common i j indent
    prev=()
    echo "."
    while IFS= read -r -d '' rel; do
        IFS='/' read -r -d '' -a parts < <(printf '%s\0' "$rel") || true
        n=${#parts[@]}

        common=0
        while [ "$common" -lt $((n - 1)) ] && [ "$common" -lt "${#prev[@]}" ] \
              && [ "${parts[$common]}" = "${prev[$common]}" ]; do
            common=$((common + 1))
        done

        for ((i = common; i < n; i++)); do
            indent="    "
            for ((j = 0; j < i; j++)); do indent="$indent    "; done
            if [ "$i" -lt $((n - 1)) ]; then
                printf '%s%s/\n' "$indent" "${parts[$i]}"
            else
                printf '%s%s\n' "$indent" "${parts[$i]}"
            fi
        done

        if [ "$n" -gt 1 ]; then
            prev=("${parts[@]:0:$((n - 1))}")
        else
            prev=()
        fi
    done < "$FILE_LIST"
}

log "$GREEN" "Starting project export..."
log "$YELLOW" "Project Path: $PROJECT_PATH"
log "$YELLOW" "Output File:  $OUTPUT_PATH"

RAW_LIST="$(mktemp)"
FILE_LIST="$(mktemp)"
TMP_OUTPUT=""
cleanup() { rm -f "$RAW_LIST" "$FILE_LIST" ${TMP_OUTPUT:+"$TMP_OUTPUT"}; }
trap cleanup EXIT

if in_git_repo; then
    log "$CYAN" "Listing files via git..."
    git ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard > "$RAW_LIST"
else
    log "$YELLOW" "Not a git repo; falling back to find..."
    find . -type f -print0 > "$RAW_LIST"
fi

while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do
    rel="${file#./}"
    [ "$rel" = "$OUTPUT_REL" ] && continue
    is_excluded_path "$rel" && continue
    is_included_file "$rel" || continue
    [ -f "$rel" ] || continue
    is_text "$rel" || continue
    printf '%s\0' "$rel"
done < "$RAW_LIST" | LC_ALL=C sort -z -u > "$FILE_LIST"

FILE_COUNT=0
while IFS= read -r -d '' _; do FILE_COUNT=$((FILE_COUNT + 1)); done < "$FILE_LIST"
log "$GREEN" "Found $FILE_COUNT files to export"

GIT_COMMIT="n/a"; GIT_BRANCH="n/a"; GIT_DIRTY="n/a"
if in_git_repo; then
    commit="$(git rev-parse --verify --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [ -n "$commit" ] && GIT_COMMIT="$commit"
    branch="$(git branch --show-current 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [ -n "$branch" ] && GIT_BRANCH="$branch"

    status_args=(status --porcelain -- . ":(exclude)$OUTPUT_REL")
    if [ -n "$(git "${status_args[@]}" 2>/dev/null || true)" ]; then
        GIT_DIRTY="yes (uncommitted changes are included below)"
    else
        GIT_DIRTY="no"
    fi
fi
DOTNET_VERSION="$(dotnet --version 2>/dev/null || echo 'not installed')"

TMP_OUTPUT="$(mktemp "$OUTPUT_DIR/.export.XXXXXX")"

{
    echo "==============================================================================="
    echo "PROJECT EXPORT"
    echo "Generated (UTC): $(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')"
    echo "Project Path:    $PROJECT_PATH"
    echo "Git Commit:      $GIT_COMMIT"
    echo "Git Branch:      $GIT_BRANCH"
    echo "Git Dirty:       $GIT_DIRTY"
    echo ".NET SDK:        $DOTNET_VERSION"
    echo "Files Exported:  $FILE_COUNT"
    echo "==============================================================================="
    echo
    echo "DIRECTORY STRUCTURE (exported files only):"
    echo "=========================================="
    echo
    render_tree
    printf '\n\n'
    echo "FILE CONTENTS:"
    echo "=============="
    echo
} > "$TMP_OUTPUT"

TOTAL_BYTES=0
CURRENT=0
while IFS= read -r -d '' rel; do
    CURRENT=$((CURRENT + 1))
    full="$PROJECT_PATH/$rel"

    size="$(wc -c < "$full" | tr -d ' ')"
    lines="$(line_count_of "$full")"
    size_kb="$(awk "BEGIN {printf \"%.2f\", $size / 1024}")"
    hash="$(sha256_of "$full")"
    modified="$(mod_time_utc_of "$full")"
    TOTAL_BYTES=$((TOTAL_BYTES + size))

    log "$CYAN" "Processing ($CURRENT/$FILE_COUNT): $rel"

    {
        echo "================================================================================"
        echo "FILE:     $rel"
        echo "SIZE:     ${size_kb} KB (${size} bytes)"
        echo "LINES:    $lines"
        echo "SHA256:   $hash"
        echo "MODIFIED: $modified (UTC)"
        echo "================================================================================"
        echo
    } >> "$TMP_OUTPUT"

    if [ -s "$full" ]; then
        cat "$full" >> "$TMP_OUTPUT" 2>/dev/null || echo "[ERROR READING FILE]" >> "$TMP_OUTPUT"
    else
        echo "[EMPTY FILE]" >> "$TMP_OUTPUT"
    fi

    printf '\n\n' >> "$TMP_OUTPUT"
done < "$FILE_LIST"

TOTAL_MB="$(awk "BEGIN {printf \"%.2f\", $TOTAL_BYTES / 1048576}")"

{
    echo "==============================================================================="
    echo "EXPORT COMPLETED (UTC): $(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')"
    echo "Total Files Exported:   $FILE_COUNT"
    echo "Total Source Size:      ${TOTAL_MB} MB (${TOTAL_BYTES} bytes)"
    echo "Output File:            $OUTPUT_PATH"
    echo "==============================================================================="
} >> "$TMP_OUTPUT"

DUMP_HASH="$(sha256_of "$TMP_OUTPUT")"
echo "DUMP SHA256 (of all lines above this one): $DUMP_HASH" >> "$TMP_OUTPUT"

chmod 0644 "$TMP_OUTPUT"
mv -f "$TMP_OUTPUT" "$OUTPUT_PATH"
TMP_OUTPUT=""

log "$GREEN" ""
log "$GREEN" "Export completed successfully!"
log "$YELLOW" "Output file: $OUTPUT_PATH"
log "$CYAN" "Total source size: ${TOTAL_MB} MB across ${FILE_COUNT} files"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# The whole site in containers behind a Cloudflare quick tunnel. Needs podman (or docker), no .NET SDK.
#
#   scripts/instance.sh up [--no-build] [--new-url]   build, start, open the tunnel, print the URL, exit
#   scripts/instance.sh url                            print the current public URL
#   scripts/instance.sh setup-code                     print the one-time code for /setup
#   scripts/instance.sh status                         what is running
#   scripts/instance.sh logs [web|postgres|tunnel] [-f]
#   scripts/instance.sh backup                         dump the database to backups/
#   scripts/instance.sh restore <file>                 restore a dump (replaces everything)
#   scripts/instance.sh down                           stop everything, keep the data
#   scripts/instance.sh reset --yes                    stop everything and delete the data
#
# A quick tunnel's URL changes whenever the tunnel restarts. Nothing on the site depends on it.
#

set -euo pipefail
source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/lib.sh"
LOG_TAG=instance
cd "$ROOT"

TUNNEL_CONTAINER="${PLAYGROUND_TUNNEL_CONTAINER:-myblazorplayground-tunnel}"
CLOUDFLARED_IMAGE="${CLOUDFLARED_IMAGE:-docker.io/cloudflare/cloudflared:latest}"
URL_WAIT="${PLAYGROUND_URL_WAIT:-120}"
READY_WAIT="${PLAYGROUND_READY_WAIT:-300}"

usage() {
    awk 'NR > 1 && /^#/ { sub(/^# ?/, ""); print; next } NR > 1 { exit }' "$0"
}

command="${1:-up}"
[[ $# -gt 0 ]] && shift

detect_engine
ensure_env
WEB_PORT="$(env_value PLAYGROUND_WEB_PORT 8090)"
TARGET="http://127.0.0.1:${WEB_PORT}"

tunnel_url() {
    "$ENGINE" logs "$TUNNEL_CONTAINER" 2>&1 | grep -oE 'https://[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.trycloudflare\.com' | tail -n 1 || true
}

tunnel_running() {
    [[ "$("$ENGINE" inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' "$TUNNEL_CONTAINER" 2>/dev/null || true)" == "true" ]]
}

wait_ready() {
    local deadline=$(( SECONDS + READY_WAIT ))
    while (( SECONDS < deadline )); do
        http_ok "${TARGET}/health/ready" && return 0
        sleep 3
    done
    return 1
}

start_tunnel() {
    local fresh="$1"
    if (( fresh )) || ! tunnel_running; then
        "$ENGINE" rm -f "$TUNNEL_CONTAINER" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
        log "opening a quick tunnel to ${TARGET}"
        "$ENGINE" run -d --name "$TUNNEL_CONTAINER" --network host --restart unless-stopped \
            "$CLOUDFLARED_IMAGE" tunnel --no-autoupdate --url "$TARGET" >/dev/null
    fi
    local deadline=$(( SECONDS + URL_WAIT )) url=""
    while (( SECONDS < deadline )); do
        url="$(tunnel_url)"
        [[ -n "$url" ]] && break
        tunnel_running || { "$ENGINE" logs "$TUNNEL_CONTAINER" >&2 || true; die "cloudflared stopped before announcing a URL."; }
        sleep 2
    done
    [[ -n "$url" ]] || die "no tunnel URL after ${URL_WAIT}s (see: $0 logs tunnel)."
    printf '%s\n' "$url"
}

setup_code() {
    "${COMPOSE[@]}" logs web 2>&1 | grep -oE 'SETUP CODE: [A-Z0-9-]+' | tail -n 1 | sed 's/SETUP CODE: //' || true
}

case "$command" in
    up)
        build=1
        fresh=0
        for arg in "$@"; do
            case "$arg" in
                --no-build) build=0 ;;
                --new-url) fresh=1 ;;
                *) die "unknown flag '$arg' (try --help)." ;;
            esac
        done
        if (( build )); then
            if git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                export SOURCE_REVISION="$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse HEAD)"
            fi
            log "building the web image"
            "${COMPOSE[@]}" build web
        fi
        log "starting postgres and web"
        "${COMPOSE[@]}" up -d postgres web
        log "waiting for ${TARGET}/health/ready"
        wait_ready || { "${COMPOSE[@]}" logs --tail 60 web >&2 || true; die "the site did not become ready in ${READY_WAIT}s."; }
        url="$(start_tunnel "$fresh")"
        code="$(setup_code)"
        cat >&2 <<BANNER

  my blazor playground is up.

  Public URL:  ${url}
  Local URL:   ${TARGET}
$( [[ -n "$code" ]] && printf '  Setup code:  %s  (open %s/setup to create the first administrator)\n' "$code" "$url" )

  The quick tunnel URL changes when the tunnel restarts. '$0 url' prints the current one.

BANNER
        printf '%s\n' "$url"
        ;;
    url)
        url="$(tunnel_url)"
        [[ -n "$url" ]] || die "no tunnel is running (try: $0 up --no-build)."
        printf '%s\n' "$url"
        ;;
    setup-code)
        code="$(setup_code)"
        [[ -n "$code" ]] || die "no setup code in the log: setup is done, or the site has not started."
        printf '%s\n' "$code"
        ;;
    status)
        "${COMPOSE[@]}" ps
        "$ENGINE" ps --filter "name=${TUNNEL_CONTAINER}"
        if http_ok "${TARGET}/health/ready"; then log "site: ready at ${TARGET}"; else warn "site: not answering at ${TARGET}"; fi
        url="$(tunnel_url)"
        [[ -n "$url" ]] && log "tunnel: ${url}"
        ;;
    logs)
        what="${1:-web}"
        shift || true
        case "$what" in
            web | postgres) "${COMPOSE[@]}" logs "$@" "$what" ;;
            tunnel) "$ENGINE" logs "$@" "$TUNNEL_CONTAINER" ;;
            *) die "logs takes web, postgres or tunnel." ;;
        esac
        ;;
    backup)
        mkdir -p "$ROOT/backups"
        file="$ROOT/backups/playground-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).dump"
        user="$(env_value POSTGRES_USER playground)"
        db="$(env_value POSTGRES_DB playground)"
        "${COMPOSE[@]}" exec -T postgres pg_dump -U "$user" -d "$db" --format=custom >"$file"
        [[ -s "$file" ]] || { rm -f "$file"; die "the dump is empty."; }
        log "wrote ${file}"
        ;;
    restore)
        file="${1:-}"
        [[ -f "$file" ]] || die "restore needs a dump file made by '$0 backup'."
        user="$(env_value POSTGRES_USER playground)"
        db="$(env_value POSTGRES_DB playground)"
        "${COMPOSE[@]}" stop web
        "${COMPOSE[@]}" exec -T postgres pg_restore -U "$user" -d "$db" --clean --if-exists --no-owner <"$file"
        "${COMPOSE[@]}" start web
        log "restored ${file}"
        ;;
    down)
        "$ENGINE" rm -f "$TUNNEL_CONTAINER" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
        "${COMPOSE[@]}" down
        ;;
    reset)
        [[ "${1:-}" == "--yes" ]] || die "reset deletes the database. Run '$0 reset --yes' if you mean it."
        "$ENGINE" rm -f "$TUNNEL_CONTAINER" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
        "${COMPOSE[@]}" down -v
        ;;
    -h | --help | help)
        usage
        ;;
    *)
        die "unknown command '$command' (try --help)."
        ;;
esac

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
ARTIFACTS="$ROOT/artifacts"
PROJECT="myblazorplayground"

export DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1
export DOTNET_NOLOGO=1
export TESTINGPLATFORM_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1

log() { printf '[%s] %s\n' "${LOG_TAG:-playground}" "$*" >&2; }
warn() { printf '[%s] warning: %s\n' "${LOG_TAG:-playground}" "$*" >&2; }
die() { printf '[%s] error: %s\n' "${LOG_TAG:-playground}" "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
step() { printf '\n==> %s\n' "$*"; }

require() {
    local tool
    for tool in "$@"; do
        command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf 'error: %s is required but was not found on PATH\n' "$tool" >&2; exit 127; }
    done
}

detect_engine() {
    if [[ -n "${CONTAINER_ENGINE:-}" ]]; then
        command -v "$CONTAINER_ENGINE" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "CONTAINER_ENGINE is '$CONTAINER_ENGINE' and that is not on PATH."
        ENGINE="$CONTAINER_ENGINE"
    elif command -v podman >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        ENGINE=podman
    elif command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        ENGINE=docker
    else
        die "need podman (preferred) or docker on PATH."
    fi

    if [[ "$ENGINE" == podman ]]; then
        if command -v podman-compose >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            COMPOSE=(podman-compose -p "$PROJECT")
        elif podman compose version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            COMPOSE=(podman compose -p "$PROJECT")
        else
            die "podman is on PATH but no compose is: install podman-compose (Debian: sudo apt install podman-compose)."
        fi
    elif docker compose version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        COMPOSE=(docker compose -p "$PROJECT")
    else
        die "docker is on PATH but 'docker compose' is not available."
    fi
}

ensure_env() {
    local env_file="$ROOT/.env"
    if [[ -f "$env_file" ]]; then
        return 0
    fi
    local password
    password="$(LC_ALL=C tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' </dev/urandom | head -c 32 || true)"
    [[ ${#password} -eq 32 ]] || die "could not generate a database password."
    sed "s/^POSTGRES_PASSWORD=.*/POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${password}/" "$ROOT/.env.example" >"$env_file"
    chmod 600 "$env_file"
    log "created .env with a random database password (keep it; the database volume is initialized with it)."
}

env_value() {
    local key="$1" fallback="$2" value
    value="$(sed -n "s/^${key}=//p" "$ROOT/.env" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1)"
    printf '%s\n' "${value:-$fallback}"
}

http_ok() {
    if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        curl -fsS -o /dev/null --max-time 5 "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1
    else
        wget -q -T 5 -O /dev/null "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1
    fi
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Build with warnings as errors, then run the .NET and JavaScript tests.
#
#   scripts/test.sh              everything; database tests use a throwaway postgres container
#   scripts/test.sh --no-db      skip the database tests
#   scripts/test.sh --no-js      skip the JavaScript tests
#
# Set PLAYGROUND_TEST_DATABASE to a connection string that may create databases to use your own server.
#

set -euo pipefail
source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/lib.sh"
LOG_TAG=test
cd "$ROOT"

use_db=1
use_js=1
for arg in "$@"; do
    case "$arg" in
        --no-db) use_db=0 ;;

using Dapper;
using Npgsql;

namespace MyBlazorPlayground.Data.Audit;

public sealed record AuditEntry(Guid? ActorId, string? ActorName, string Action, string SubjectType, string SubjectId, string Summary, string? Client = null);

public sealed class AuditRecord
{
    public Guid Id { get; init; }

    public long Seq { get; init; }

    public DateTime OccurredAt { get; init; }

    public string? ActorName { get; init; }

    public string Action { get; init; } = string.Empty;

    public string SubjectType { get; init; } = string.Empty;

    public string SubjectId { get; init; } = string.Empty;

    public string Summary { get; init; } = string.Empty;
}

public sealed class AuditLog(Database database)
{
    private const string Insert =
        """
        INSERT INTO audit_event (id, actor_id, actor_name, action, subject_type, subject_id, summary, client)
        VALUES (@id, @ActorId, @ActorName, @Action, @SubjectType, @SubjectId, @Summary, @Client)
        """;

    public async Task WriteAsync(AuditEntry entry, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
    {
        await using var connection = await database.OpenAsync(cancellationToken);
        await WriteAsync(connection, null, entry, cancellationToken);
    }

    public static Task WriteAsync(NpgsqlConnection connection, NpgsqlTransaction? transaction, AuditEntry entry, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(connection);
        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(entry);
        return connection.ExecuteAsync(new CommandDefinition(
            Insert,
            new { id = Guid.CreateVersion7(), entry.ActorId, entry.ActorName, entry.Action, entry.SubjectType, entry.SubjectId, entry.Summary, entry.Client },
            transaction,
            cancellationToken: cancellationToken));
    }

    public async Task<IReadOnlyList<AuditRecord>> ListAsync(int limit, long? before, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
    {
        await using var connection = await database.OpenAsync(cancellationToken);
        return (await connection.QueryAsync<AuditRecord>(new CommandDefinition(
            """
            SELECT id, seq, occurred_at, actor_name, action, subject_type, subject_id, summary
            FROM audit_event
            WHERE @before::bigint IS NULL OR seq < @before::bigint
            ORDER BY seq DESC
            LIMIT @limit
            """,
            new { limit, before },
            cancellationToken: cancellationToken))).AsList();
    }
}

using Dapper;
using Npgsql;

namespace MyBlazorPlayground.Data;

public sealed class Database
{
    static Database()
    {
        DefaultTypeMap.MatchNamesWithUnderscores = true;
    }

    private readonly NpgsqlDataSource _source;

    public Database(NpgsqlDataSource source)
    {
        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(source);
        _source = source;
    }

    public NpgsqlConnection Open() => _source.OpenConnection();

    public ValueTask<NpgsqlConnection> OpenAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) =>
        _source.OpenConnectionAsync(cancellationToken);

    public async Task<T> InTransactionAsync<T>(Func<NpgsqlConnection, NpgsqlTransaction, Task<T>> work, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
    {
        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(work);
        await using var connection = await OpenAsync(cancellationToken);
        await using var transaction = await connection.BeginTransactionAsync(cancellationToken);
        var result = await work(connection, transaction);
        await transaction.CommitAsync(cancellationToken);
        return result;
    }

    public static bool IsUniqueViolation(Exception exception) =>
        exception is PostgresException { SqlState: PostgresErrorCodes.UniqueViolation };
}

using System.Reflection;
using System.Text.RegularExpressions;
using Dapper;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
using Npgsql;

namespace MyBlazorPlayground.Data;

public sealed partial class MigrationRunner(Database database, ILogger<MigrationRunner> logger)
{
    private const long LockKey = 0x6D79_626C_617A_6F72;

    public static IReadOnlyList<Migration> Embedded()
    {
        var assembly = typeof(MigrationRunner).Assembly;
        var migrations = new List<Migration>();
        foreach (var name in assembly.GetManifestResourceNames())
        {
            var match = ResourcePattern().Match(name);
            if (!match.Success)
            {
                continue;
            }

            using var stream = assembly.GetManifestResourceStream(name)
                ?? throw new InvalidOperationException($"Missing resource {name}.");
            using var reader = new StreamReader(stream);
            migrations.Add(new Migration(int.Parse(match.Groups[1].Value, System.Globalization.CultureInfo.InvariantCulture), match.Groups[2].Value, reader.ReadToEnd()));
        }

        var ordered = migrations.OrderBy(migration => migration.Version).ToList();
        if (ordered.Select(migration => migration.Version).Distinct().Count() != ordered.Count)
        {
            throw new InvalidOperationException("Two migrations share a version number.");
        }

        return ordered;
    }

    public async Task RunAsync(int attempts, TimeSpan delay, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        for (var attempt = 1; ; attempt++)
        {
            try
            {
                await ApplyAsync(cancellationToken);
                return;
            }
            catch (NpgsqlException exception) when (attempt < attempts && IsTransient(exception))
            {
                LogWaiting(logger, attempt, attempts, exception.Message);
                await Task.Delay(delay, cancellationToken);
            }
        }
    }

    private static bool IsTransient(NpgsqlException exception) =>
        exception is not PostgresException postgres
        || postgres.SqlState is PostgresErrorCodes.CannotConnectNow or PostgresErrorCodes.AdminShutdown;

    private async Task ApplyAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        await using var connection = await database.OpenAsync(cancellationToken);
        await connection.ExecuteAsync(new CommandDefinition("SELECT pg_advisory_lock(@key)", new { key = LockKey }, cancellationToken: cancellationToken));
        try
        {
            await connection.ExecuteAsync(new CommandDefinition(
                """
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_migration (
                    version integer PRIMARY KEY,
                    name text NOT NULL,
                    applied_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
                )
                """,
                cancellationToken: cancellationToken));
            var applied = (await connection.QueryAsync<int>(new CommandDefinition("SELECT version FROM schema_migration", cancellationToken: cancellationToken))).ToHashSet();
            foreach (var migration in Embedded().Where(migration => !applied.Contains(migration.Version)))
            {
                await using var transaction = await connection.BeginTransactionAsync(cancellationToken);
                await connection.ExecuteAsync(new CommandDefinition(migration.Sql, transaction: transaction, cancellationToken: cancellationToken));
                await connection.ExecuteAsync(new CommandDefinition(
                    "INSERT INTO schema_migration (version, name) VALUES (@Version, @Name)",
                    new { migration.Version, migration.Name },
                    transaction,
                    cancellationToken: cancellationToken));
                await transaction.CommitAsync(cancellationToken);
                LogApplied(logger, migration.Version, migration.Name);
            }
        }
        finally
        {
            await connection.ExecuteAsync(new CommandDefinition("SELECT pg_advisory_unlock(@key)", new { key = LockKey }, cancellationToken: CancellationToken.None));
        }
    }

    [GeneratedRegex(@"^Migrations/(\d{4})_([a-z0-9_]+)\.sql$")]
    private static partial Regex ResourcePattern();

    [LoggerMessage(Level = LogLevel.Warning, Message = "Database not reachable yet (attempt {Attempt} of {Attempts}): {Reason}")]
    private static partial void LogWaiting(ILogger logger, int attempt, int attempts, string reason);

    [LoggerMessage(Level = LogLevel.Information, Message = "Applied migration {Version} {Name}")]
    private static partial void LogApplied(ILogger logger, int version, string name);
}

public sealed record Migration(int Version, string Name, string Sql);

using Dapper;

namespace MyBlazorPlayground.Data.Nest;

public sealed class NestEntryRecord
{
    public Guid Id { get; init; }

    public string Kind { get; init; } = string.Empty;

    public string[] Keys { get; init; } = [];

    public string? Url { get; init; }

    public string? Fields { get; init; }

    public string? Text { get; init; }

    public DateTime? DeletedAt { get; init; }
}

public sealed record NestEntryRow(Guid Id, string Kind, string[] Keys, string? Url, string? Fields, string? Text);

public sealed class NestEntryStore(Database database)
{
    public async Task<IReadOnlyList<NestEntryRecord>> LoadAsync(int limit, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
    {
        await using var connection = await database.OpenAsync(cancellationToken);
        return (await connection.QueryAsync<NestEntryRecord>(new CommandDefinition(
            """
            (SELECT id, kind, keys, url, fields::text AS fields, text, deleted_at FROM nest_entry WHERE deleted_at IS NULL ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT @limit)
            UNION ALL
            (SELECT id, kind, keys, NULL, NULL, NULL, deleted_at FROM nest_entry WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL)
            """,
            new { limit },
            cancellationToken: cancellationToken))).AsList();
    }

    public async Task<int> InsertAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<NestEntryRow> rows, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
    {
        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(rows);
        if (rows.Count == 0)
        {
            return 0;
        }

        return await database.InTransactionAsync(async (connection, transaction) =>
        {
            var inserted = 0;
            foreach (var row in rows)
            {
                inserted += await connection.ExecuteAsync(new CommandDefinition(
                    """
                    INSERT INTO nest_entry (id, kind, keys, url, fields, text)
                    VALUES (@Id, @Kind, @Keys, @Url, @Fields::jsonb, @Text)
                    ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING
                    """,
                    row,
                    transaction,
                    cancellationToken: cancellationToken));
            }

            return inserted;
        }, cancellationToken);
    }

    public async Task<IReadOnlyList<NestEntryRecord>> ForKeysAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<string> keys, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
    {
        await using var connection = await database.OpenAsync(cancellationToken);
        return (await connection.QueryAsync<NestEntryRecord>(new CommandDefinition(
            "SELECT id, kind, keys, url, fields::text AS fields, text, deleted_at FROM nest_entry WHERE keys && @keys ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 2000",
            new { keys = keys.ToArray() },
            cancellationToken: cancellationToken))).AsList();
    }

    public async Task<NestEntryRecord?> FindAsync(Guid id, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
    {
        await using var connection = await database.OpenAsync(cancellationToken);
        return await connection.QuerySingleOrDefaultAsync<NestEntryRecord>(new CommandDefinition(
            "SELECT id, kind, keys, url, fields::text AS fields, text, deleted_at FROM nest_entry WHERE id = @id",
            new { id },
            cancellationToken: cancellationToken));
    }
}

using Dapper;

namespace MyBlazorPlayground.Data.Pages;

public sealed class PageEditorRecord
{
    public string PageKey { get; init; } = string.Empty;

    public Guid PersonId { get; init; }

    public string UserName { get; init; } = string.Empty;

    public string DisplayName { get; init; } = string.Empty;

    public DateTime GrantedAt { get; init; }
}

public sealed class PageEditorStore(Database database)
{
    public async Task<bool> IsEditorAsync(Guid personId, IReadOnlyCollection<string> pageKeys, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
    {
        if (pageKeys.Count == 0)
        {
            return false;
        }

        await using var connection = await database.OpenAsync(cancellationToken);
        return await connection.ExecuteScalarAsync<bool>(new CommandDefinition(
            "SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM page_editor WHERE person_id = @personId AND page_key = ANY(@keys))",
            new { personId, keys = pageKeys.ToArray() },
            cancellationToken: cancellationToken));
    }

    public async Task<IReadOnlyList<PageEditorRecord>> ListAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
    {
        await using var connection = await database.OpenAsync(cancellationToken);
        return (await connection.QueryAsync<PageEditorRecord>(new CommandDefinition(
            """
            SELECT e.page_key, e.person_id, p.user_name, p.display_name, e.granted_at
            FROM page_editor e JOIN person p ON p.id = e.person_id
            ORDER BY e.page_key, p.user_name
            """,
            cancellationToken: cancellationToken))).AsList();
    }

    public async Task<bool> GrantAsync(string pageKey, Guid personId, Guid grantedBy, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
    {
        await using var connection = await database.OpenAsync(cancellationToken);
        return await connection.ExecuteAsync(new CommandDefinition(
            "INSERT INTO page_editor (page_key, person_id, granted_by) VALUES (@pageKey, @personId, @grantedBy) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING",
            new { pageKey, personId, grantedBy },
            cancellationToken: cancellationToken)) > 0;
    }

    public async Task<bool> RevokeAsync(string pageKey, Guid personId, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
    {

            "DELETE FROM page_editor WHERE page_key = @pageKey AND person_id = @personId",
            new { pageKey, personId },
            cancellationToken: cancellationToken)) > 0;
    }

using Dapper;

public sealed class PersonRecord
